Note: Real BC writes the output of publishing the system app into the application database, so the Metadata BLOB on Object Metadata (2000000071) carries a payload; a real service tier confirmed that, on every leg of StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#179 (BC 27.0-28.4, Cloud and OnPrem), which is merged and is the commit this repo's corpus pin already carries. The runner has no application database and publishes nothing into one, so it has no source for that column. It used to hand back BC's own default - a 0-byte BLOB indistinguishable from a legitimately empty one - and this entry was expect-divergence for exactly that answer. Since #2771 the read is REFUSED by name instead (RecordPatches.NoSourceColumns), which is an out-of-scope signal. WHY expect-oos, AND WHAT THE CLASSIFIER DOES NOT DECIDE FOR YOU: expect-divergence is ruled out mechanically - it means 'answers differently and does NOT signal', so the classifier fails it with 'Declare it expect-oos instead', and it did, on all eight legs. expect-fail-known-gap is NOT ruled out mechanically: that mode accepts any non-pass result, and flipping this entry to it was MEASURED to go green (exit 0, pass-known-gap 1). It is rejected on meaning, not on mechanism. That mode means 'in scope, not built yet, Issue tracks the work', and its authoring rule requires an issue that is open at PR time and stays open after merge. The only candidate here is #2771, which this PR closes - so the entry would point at a closed issue the moment it merged, the exact bookkeeping lie docs/expectations.md names. Nothing is owed: the runner will never publish into an application database. WHY THE ANCHOR IS not-yet-implemented AND NOT A docs/scope.md SECTION: it is not a promise to implement. The throw site emits 'not-yet-implemented - object-metadata-payload - ...' and ExpectationManifest.ReasonAnchor cuts at the first em-dash, so the anchor is what this entry carries. ApplicationObjectBasePatches.IsPermanentOutOfScope is !Reason.StartsWith("not-yet-implemented"), and a refusal it calls permanent is trapped into false for an AL [TryFunction]. Trapping is faithful where real BC also lacks the surface; a tier DOES answer this one, so trapping would restore the silent default the refusal exists to remove (.claude/rules/loud-failures.md). The anchor buys the tear-through. That it says 'yet' about something permanent is a genuine vocabulary gap, tracked in #3154 - the runner has no anchor meaning 'permanent, but a tier does answer it'.
